chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described, and how can He be described?
And He said in His Book: 'And they did not estimate Allah with the estimation that is due to Him,' so He would not be described with any estimation except that it would be less than that.

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cannot be described, and how can one describe a servant whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has veiled with seven (veils), and made obedience to him on earth like obedience to Him in the sky?

So He said: 'And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and from whatever he forbids you, keep back,' and 'Whoever obeys this one has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me,' and He delegated authority to him.
And we cannot be described, and how can one describe a group of people whom Allah has removed the filth from, and it is doubt?

And the believer cannot be described. And indeed, when a believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, Allah does not cease looking at them both, and sins fall from their faces just as leaves fall from the tree.

key_terms.حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: With the estimation that is due to Him

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of shaking hands between believers in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of *la yuwsaf* (inexpressibility), extending the transcendence of Allah to the Prophet, the Imams, and the general believer, thereby elevating their spiritual status beyond human limitation. It uniquely links the theological concept of divine veiling (*hijab*) with the practical ethic of brotherhood, illustrating that physical gestures like handshaking serve as mechanisms for the shedding of sins, a theme resonating with the Quranic imagery of leaves falling from trees.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic cannot be described.

And how can Heazwj be described, and Heazwj Says in Hisazwj Book [22:74] They are not estimating Allah with the estimation that is due to Him. Thus, Heasws would not be estimated except that Heazwj would be Greater than that.

And the Prophetsaww cannot be described. How can one describe a servant whom Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Veiled by seven (veils), and Made obedience to himsaww in the earth like being obedient to Himazwj in the sky, so Heazwj Said [59:7] and whatever the Rasool gives you, accept it, and from whatever he forbids you, keep back, and the one who obeys this one so he has obeyed Meazwj, and the one who disobeys himsaww, so he has disobeyed Meazwj, and Authorised himsaww.
And weasws cannot be described. And how can one describe a group of people whom Allahazwj has Kept the filth away from themasws, and is there (any) doubt (in it)?. And a Momin cannot be described.
And a Momin meets his brother and shakes his hand, so Allahazwj does not Cease looking at them both, and sins erode from their faces just as the leaves erode from the tree’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Rib’i from Zurara who has said

the following: “I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, cannot be described and how can He be described when He says in His book, “They have not revered (honored and respected) Allah properly. . . .” [22:74] He cannot be described through measurement. He is greater than such measures of respect.

The Holy Prophet cannot be described and respected. How can a servant (of Allah) be described whom Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has veiled with seven things (no explanation for this seven is available). He has made obedience to him on earth like the obedience to His own self in heavens saying, ‘Take only what the Messenger gives to you and desist from what he forbids you,’ [59:7] whoever obeys him has obeyed Me and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me. He (Allah) made him to be the in charge person of the affairs.
We also cannot be described and how can a people be described from whom Allah has removed all rijs (uncleanness), which, applies to doubt (doubt is uncleanness).

The believing people also cannot be described. When the believer meets his brother (in belief) and they shake hands Allah continues looking at them and the sins fall from their faces like leaves fall off trees.’”
